title: Basilisk: Using Provenance Invariants to Automate Proofs of Undecidable Protocols
problem: Verifying correctness of distributed protocols is challenging, especially for undecidable protocols where no complete algorithmic proof procedure exists. Manual proof construction is labor-intensive and error-prone.
motivation: Automated protocol verification reduces manual effort and improves system reliability by enabling formal correctness assurances for complex distributed systems.
method: Basilisk uses provenance invariants—properties tracking data flow origins through protocol states—to guide automated proof generation. The system encodes protocol semantics and invariants into constraint-satisfaction formulations, leveraging automated solvers to generate proofs even for theoretically undecidable protocol classes by discovering structural properties.
key_novelty: Applying provenance tracking as an automated proof basis for protocols that are theoretically undecidable by conventional methods.
contributions: Provenance-based framework for automated protocol verification
Techniques for automating proofs of undecidable protocols via invariant discovery
Basilisk tool implementation for provenance-guided proof generation
